segments: The Eighteenth Dynasties of the Arab Kings.
349 of the Arabs [960–961 AD]:
When the Egyptians who were going to pray in Mecca were returning,
they encamped in a certain valley in which water had not flowed for a long time.
And at night, while they were sleeping,
a flash flood came down,
and swept them all away together with their baggage,
and cast them into the great sea,
and they all perished.
And in this year,
about two hundred thousand tents of the Turks who were in the east submitted and converted to the religion of the Arabs.
And in the year 350,
350 of the Arabs [961–962 AD]:
a great caravan of the Arabs set out from Antioch towards Tarsus,
and ambushes of the Romans fell upon them,
and killed some of them,
and led away the rest as prisoners, a great multitude.
And the Arabs were enraged;
and Najā, the slave of Sayf al-Dawla, entered the territory of the Romans from the region of Mayperqat [Martyropolis],
and took great spoil, together with two thousand people,
and five hundred of them he bound in chains and brought out with him.
And in the year 1274,
1274 of the Greeks [962–963 AD]:
the Domesticus [came] with one hundred and sixty thousand horsemen to Cilicia,
and encamped against Anazarbus,
and waged a fierce battle against it.
And when the Arabs inside despaired of help coming to them,
they asked for a pledge of safe conduct for their lives and their property, that they might surrender the fortress,
especially when they saw that those from the side of the mountain were close to breaching the wall.
Then Nicephorus gave them a pledge,
and they opened the fortress.
And when he entered and saw that they had been close to opening it by the sword without toil,
he regretted having given them a pledge.
And he commanded that all the people be gathered into the mosque,
and that whoever did not enter the mosque, his blood would be upon his own head.
Then, on the morning of the [next] day, the infantry who were with him entered the city,
and everyone whom they found in house and street they killed, men, women, and children.
And he collected all the weapons that were in the city,
for there were found in it forty thousand coats of mail, that is, cuirasses alone,
apart from a great multitude of swords and bows.
And they cut down forty thousand palm trees.
And he commanded that those who were in the mosque should go out and go wherever they wished,
and whoever remained until the evening should be killed.
